title: Escalating Violent Crackdown in Azad Kashmir Triggers Global Calls for Media Access and Independent Inquiry

body.text: The United Kashmir People’s National Party (UKPNP) has issued an urgent international appeal condemning what it termed a direct assault on democratic rights and a 'massacre' of unarmed civilians, following deadly clashes between security forces and protesters in Rawalakot, the capital of Poonch district.

The violence reached a critical juncture late on the night of June 7, when security forces reportedly opened direct fire on demonstrators who had gathered outside the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Rawalakot. The crowd had assembled following the death of local political activist Shahzaib Habib, who was killed in a targeted attack on June 5 near Barmanag while returning from Khaigala.

Peaceful protest is a democratic right. Pakistan must immediately halt this cycle of tyranny against unarmed Kashmiris in the disputed state. We appeal to the United Nations and the international community to intervene.
SEQUENCE OF EVENTS: FROM TARGETED AMBUSH TO FUNERAL FIRING

According to local activist groups and leaders of the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), security forces deployed live ammunition and tear gas against mourners and demonstrators, resulting in multiple civilian casualties. Local health officials and human rights watchdogs confirm significant casualties and injuries, while over 350 residents have reportedly been detained in regional raids.

items: June 5: Vehicle targeted near Barmanag; Shahzaib Habib killed and JAAC leader Umar Nazir injured
June 6–7: Mass arrests across districts, telecommunications blackout imposed, and JAAC banned under anti-terror laws
June 7 Night: Security forces open fire outside Rawalakot CMH Hospital during protest assembly
June 8: UKPNP issues global appeal to the UN, Amnesty International, and international news outlets

body.text: UKPNP Chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri strongly condemned the initial targeted attack on June 5, offering condolences to Habib's family and wishing Nazir a swift recovery. Tensions escalated dramatically when thousands gathered outside the CMH mortuary for Habib's funeral prayers and to demand accountability.
BAN ON JAAC AND INFORMATION BLACKOUT CONCERNS

The outbreak of violence follows a move by local authorities on June 5 to proscribe the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) under anti-terrorism legislation. The government implemented a region-wide telecommunications blackout, suspending mobile internet services across multiple districts, alongside sweeping arrests targeting rights organizers.

Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri characterized the proscription as a 'draconian and undemocratic measure' aimed at silencing civil dissent. He highlighted that the sudden ban marks a sharp policy reversal, given that representatives from the Government of Pakistan and the local Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) administration had been engaged in direct negotiations with JAAC leadership only days earlier.

items: 12 Reserved Refugee Seats: JAAC demands abolition; Supreme Court ruled seats are constitutionally protected
Anti-Terror Designation: Activists argue the ban suppresses rights; authorities cite public disruption concerns
Information Blackout: Residents raise concerns over blackouts; authorities cite security and anti-misinformation measures

body.text: During negotiations, officials referred to JAAC representatives as brothers. The sudden reclassification of the organization as a terrorist entity raises serious questions and warrants an immediate review.
APPEALS FOR INTERNATIONAL COVERAGE AND RESTRAINT

In light of ongoing information restrictions, the UKPNP leadership appealed directly to international media organizations—including the BBC, Al Jazeera, Deutsche Welle (DW), RT, and France 24—as well as international human rights watchdogs, urging them to send correspondents to Rawalakot and surrounding areas to verify facts on the ground.

The UKPNP reaffirmed its commitment to nonviolent advocacy, praising Umar Nazir's public calls for calm despite his personal grief. The party also issued a directive to its members and the public to refrain from circulating unverified reports, manipulated audio, or AI-generated media, urging reliance solely on official, verified party channels while the central leadership continues to monitor developments.

items: Urgent demand for unhindered access for international media and independent fact-finders
Immediate lifting of mobile internet and cellular communication blackouts
Release of nonviolent political activists detained during regional sweeps
Full adherence to international standards under the UDHR and ICCPR covenants
